prompt.brief: Design a confidential-computing platform that protects sensitive data while it is processed, attests the workload and code identity, and releases keys only to an approved trusted execution environment.
successSignals: Define workload images, measurements, attestation claims, tenant keys, and encrypted input/output as the trust boundary.
Make key release conditional on hardware attestation, policy version, identity, region, and approved code measurement.
Keep plaintext inside the enclave or confidential VM and minimize host, operator, logging, and debugging exposure.
Explain enclave failure, key rotation, side-channel risk, performance cost, audit evidence, and safe recovery.

functional: Register approved workloads, upload encrypted inputs, request attestation, release scoped keys, and run confidential jobs.
Expose job state, measurement, attestation result, policy decision, resource usage, and encrypted output retrieval.
Support tenant isolation, key rotation and revocation, workload upgrades, deletion, audit export, and incident quarantine.
nonFunctional: Keep sensitive plaintext out of host memory, ordinary logs, crash dumps, and operator access by policy.
Scale attestation and key-release decisions without one tenant key or policy service becoming a hot dependency.
Never release keys to an unapproved measurement; make job retries safe without duplicating external effects.
Fail closed for key release while preserving encrypted inputs, audit events, and resumable job state.
scaleAssumptions: Support 1,000 confidential jobs per minute across multiple regions and regulated tenant partitions.
Partition key-release policy by tenant and workload measurement; isolate large jobs and attestation bursts.
Retain encrypted inputs, signed attestations, policy decisions, and audit evidence while keeping enclave state ephemeral.

dataFlow.title: Accept Protect data during processing
dataFlow.description: The Confidential-computing platform gateway authenticates the caller, validates the request, applies tenant policy and idempotency, then routes it to the owning service.

dataFlow.title: Commit the durable state
dataFlow.description: The control plane records a workload, image, policy, and attestation requirement before releasing protected data.

dataFlow.title: Publish the domain event
dataFlow.description: A durable outbox publishes committed Confidential-computing platform events; consumers deduplicate by event ID and track offsets.

dataFlow.title: Build the read model
dataFlow.description: Partitioned workers consume Confidential-computing platform events, update the serving projection, and expose lag or watermark metadata.

dataFlow.title: Serve and recover asynchronously
dataFlow.description: Serving reads use the Confidential-computing platform projection; replay, repair, export, and slow work remain off the request path.

architecture.title: Design a secure compute environment that protects data in use with hardware-based encryption, verifies compute integrity, and manages encryption keys securely. reference architecture
architecture.summary: The authoritative state records Protect data during processing; asynchronous workers build serving projections while Confidential VMs with SGX/SEV, Azure Attestation for verification, Key Vault with HSM stays isolated from the request path.

deepDives.title: Consistency and idempotency
points: Keep the Confidential-computing platform commit authoritative; let derived projections converge with visible version and freshness.
Use idempotency keys, conditional Confidential-computing platform writes, event IDs, and versions so retries and replay are safe.
Return Confidential-computing platform version and observedAt so clients can reason about freshness.

deepDives.title: Partitioning and hot keys
points: Partition Confidential-computing platform by its primary read and write keys, then isolate hot tenants, users, items, or regions.
Bound Confidential-computing platform work with backpressure and queue isolation so one hot key cannot dominate the cluster.
Keep a replay or reconciliation path for Confidential-computing platform projection drift and partial failures.

deepDives.title: Failure and recovery
points: Serve the last acceptable Confidential-computing platform projection or an explicit degraded response when workers fail.
Retain durable Confidential-computing platform records for replay and make each downstream effect independently retryable.
Measure Confidential-computing platform latency, backlog, freshness, error rate, and correctness drift.

tradeoffs.title: Strong consistency versus throughput
tradeoffs.recommendation: Strongly protect the business commit and use versioned eventual projections for high-volume reads.
tradeoffs.caution: Making every derived read synchronous increases coordination and tail latency.

tradeoffs.title: Push versus pull processing
tradeoffs.recommendation: Push bounded events to workers and pull durable snapshots on reads or recovery.
tradeoffs.caution: Unbounded fanout or full scans make bursts and hot keys expensive.

tradeoffs.title: Managed service versus custom control
tradeoffs.recommendation: Start with managed primitives where their limits match the access pattern, then isolate replaceable interfaces.
tradeoffs.caution: Provider defaults do not remove the need for quotas, replay, observability, and data lifecycle design.

commonMistakes: Putting all work on the synchronous request path.
Choosing a data store before writing the access patterns and consistency contract.
Ignoring retries, duplicate events, late data, deletion, privacy, or authorization.
Leaving hot partitions, backpressure, stale reads, and recovery unspecified.
Allowing unbounded requests or exports to compete with normal traffic.

followUps.question: What happens when the primary worker is unavailable?
followUps.answer: Acknowledge only after the durable boundary, serve the last acceptable projection, queue retryable work, and replay or reconcile after recovery.

followUps.question: How would you support a tenfold traffic spike?
followUps.answer: Pre-scale partitions, apply admission control and backpressure, isolate hot keys, cache immutable snapshots, and make freshness degradation visible.

followUps.question: How do you verify correctness?
followUps.answer: Use idempotency metrics, version gaps, sampled source-to-projection comparisons, replay tests, and a shadow rebuild before repair.

rubric.description: The answer defines protected workload setup, attestation, key release, execution, auditability, and failure contracts.
Entities and workload/measurement keys support confidentiality, attestation, key release, audit, privacy, and lifecycle changes.
Partitioning, cache behavior, queues, backpressure, and hot-key handling are explicit.
Idempotency, replay, recovery, degraded reads, and observability protect committed state.
The candidate can explain Confidential-computing platform consistency, push/pull, managed services, and the scale boundary.
